answer: Sybil resistance can come from a liveness pulse: every identity must regularly complete verified useful work, a heartbeat of service delivered to counterparties, or its standing decays to zero. An island of fake accounts cannot be created and left idle; each must keep pulsing, trade after trade, to stay trusted. Docking at a new jetty of services requires an unbroken pulse history, so an attacker with a thousand fakes must continuously fund a thousand streams of real work, and the moment any stream stops, that identity's reputation withers. The cost is not one-time but forever recurring.
